signals.notes: ICSG world refined copper USAGE growth for 2026 cut to +1.6% from +2.1% (Oct-2025 forecast); 2027 +2.0%. China +1.9%, rest of world +1.3%. Segment sum-check passes: 0.58x1.9 + 0.42x1.3 = 1.65% vs the 1.6% world figure. Level is DERIVED, not a filed ICSG level: 27.4 Mt world usage in 2024 [ICSG World Copper Factbook 2025] x 1.03 (2025) x 1.016 (2026) = ~28.67 Mt, labelled inference. Required series copper.refined-balance and copper.energy-transition-demand are UNAVAILABLE; this row is unvintaged secondary reporting of ICSG and cannot lift sufficiency.

REALISED, not forecast: world apparent refined copper usage grew only +0.8% y/y in Q1-2026, half the +1.6% full-year forecast ICSG carries; global cathode production grew ~4.5% over the same window. China apparent demand EXCLUDING bonded/unreported inventory change was 'basically flat' (~0%). Falsifiable bar printed: for the full year to reach +1.6%, the remaining nine months must run ~+1.9% ((1.6x12 - 0.8x3)/9 = 1.87%), more than twice the realised Q1 rate. Deliberately linked to the Jan-Apr China row as an opposing fact rather than averaged (CLAUDE.md 3). Note the definitional difference IS the contradiction: this figure strips the bonded-stock change and the other does not.

The opposing fact, emitted separately: China apparent refined copper demand +2.4% over Jan-Apr 2026, with China refined production +7.4% and China net refined imports -25% over the same window (domestic smelters displacing imports rather than incremental consumption). Weaker source tier than the Q1 row (a secondary summary, not the ICSG release), different window (4 months vs 3) and a different definition (does not strip bonded/unreported stock change). Binding COPPER family rule honoured: China activity is a demand INPUT and is NOT proof of copper demand without a primary end-use or refined-balance series - I hold neither with an accepted vintage, so this row does not become a China demand verdict.

Explicit gap row so the absence is machine-visible, zero strength, non-voting. The required row needs a grid + EV + renewable bridge from PRIMARY deployment data (GW commissioned, EV units) x PRIMARY intensity coefficients (t Cu/GW, t Cu/vehicle). Neither leg is reachable. What exists is ratio colour (EV ~3-4x an ICE car; renewables ~2.5-7x fossil generation) and 2040 SCENARIO shares (clean energy ~50-61% of copper demand under more ambitious IEA scenarios) - a 2040 scenario share is not 2026 consumption. Double-counting rule honoured: ICSG world refined usage (~28.67 Mt derived, 2026) ALREADY contains every grid/EV/renewable tonne, so any transition figure would be a decomposition of it, never an addition. Consequence: copper's stated structural strategic thesis is unmeasured by this orb.

The reason copper.refined-balance is marked UNAVAILABLE rather than carried at +96 kt. Attribution (MODULE_RULES 4a): ICSG 2026 refined PRODUCTION growth +0.4% and USAGE growth +1.6% x 2025 base levels of ~28.44 Mt / ~28.22 Mt (my arithmetic, compounding ICSG 2024 actuals 27.5/27.4 Mt by reported 2025 growth +3.4%/+3.0%) = an implied 2026 balance of 28.55 - 28.67 = -125 kt, a DEFICIT, against the +96 kt SURPLUS headline from the same reported release -> 0% explained; the two disagree by 221 kt and point in OPPOSITE directions. Method check: the same arithmetic on 2025 gives +213 kt vs ICSG's reported +178 kt, a 35 kt gap, so the method is sound to within rounding and the 221 kt gap is a real inconsistency in the reported figures. Under CLAUDE.md 5 neither number may be published as the balance. Direction neutral BECAUSE the sign is unresolved - this is not a weak surplus call.

Realised ICSG Q1-2026 world refined balance: +396 kt oversupply (386 kt seasonally adjusted for Chinese bonded-warehouse inventory change), against +135 kt in Q1-2025 - nearly 3x. Implied-arithmetic finding: Q1 alone is 4x the +96 kt full-year forecast, so 96 - 396 = -300 kt is implied for Apr-Dec 2026, i.e. a 300 kt DEFICIT over nine months (-33 kt/month) after a Q1 running +132 kt/month surplus, a ~165 kt/month swing. CAVEAT that stops this being binding: I could not establish whether the +96 kt forecast was struck before or after the 2026-05-23 Q1 print (the forecast-meeting date is not stated in any reachable secondary source; the carrying article published 2026-06-30). If the forecast predates the Q1 data the -300 kt implication is a vintage-mixing artefact. Recorded as suggestive, not proven. Attribution (4a) linking surplus to stock: +396 kt (3-month FLOW basis) x 1.0 = +396 kt of the +401 kt three-exchange visible build from end-2025 to end-May-2026 -> PERIOD MISMATCH, a 3-month flow against a 5-month stock change; at face value 99% but on a matched basis the Apr-May surplus is unsourced so the true share is UNKNOWN. What it does establish: the surplus is landing in VISIBLE exchange stocks, not vanishing into unmeasured inventory.

The AGGREGATE buffer is comfortable, not tight. Combined three-exchange visible stock ~968.4 kt = LME total 235.6 kt (2026-08-27) + COMEX registered+eligible 745,277 short tons = 676.1 kt at 0.90718474 t/st (2026-08-25) + SHFE warrant 56.7 kt (2026-08-19). That is +30.1% vs end-2025 (744.1 kt) and -15.4% vs end-May-2026 (1,145.0 kt). Placed vs history: LME total sits at the 46th PERCENTILE of a 19-year record - mid-range - off a 2026 peak of 402.6 kt and +77 kt higher than 12 months ago. Cover: 968.4 kt / 551.4 kt per week (world usage ~28.67 Mt/yr derived) = 1.76 weeks = 12.3 DAYS; stocks-to-use 3.38%. HEALTH WARNINGS, without which the total is not a measurement: timestamps span 8 days in a week when LME on-warrant moved 36%; COMEX Grade 1, LME Grade A and SHFE (VAT/bonded regime) are different eligibility lists and are added here as a labelled approximation, contrary to the strict reading of the COPPER family rule.

The opposing fact, emitted separately rather than netted: the DELIVERABLE slice is thin. Warrant status separated per the binding COPPER family rule. LME on-warrant/available 107.05 kt on 2026-08-27, DOWN 35.8% in one week from 166.775 kt on 2026-08-20 = 1.4 DAYS of world consumption. LME cancelled warrants 121.4 kt on 2026-08-21 = 50.52% of a ~240.3 kt total, a +73.45% one-day jump and +21.19pp on the ratio, so half of what remains is already earmarked to leave, reportedly from US and Asian free-trade-zone warehouses with the metal likely bound INTO the US. On-warrant tier across venues: LME 107.05 + COMEX registered 415.5 kt (458.0k short tons, 2026-08-03, 63.7% of total - note 22-day staleness) + SHFE warrant 56.7 kt = 579.3 kt = 7.4 days, stocks-to-use 2.02%. Applying the stale 63.7% ratio to the fresher 2026-08-25 COMEX total instead gives ~594.4 kt / 7.6 days - shown only as a check because that is a stale ratio on a fresh level, i.e. inference; the conclusion is identical. NO percentile is emitted for the on-warrant sub-series: no history is held, so it is placed by CHANGE, not by rank. Corroborating cross-module fact, NOT emitted by me: LME cash-3M backwardation ~US$248-254/t, owned by commodity-price-curve.

The reconciling fact between the two rows above: it is the same metal in the wrong place. 676.1 / 968.4 = 69.8% of visible stock sits in COMEX/US warehouses. Ex-US (LME total 235.6 + SHFE warrant 56.7) = 292.3 kt = 3.7 DAYS of world consumption, stocks-to-use 1.02%. Cause is cross-referenced, NOT voted: the Section 232 tariff threat on refined cathode (50% already on semi-finished; cathode exempt but a phased 15% from Jan-2027 rising to 30% in Jan-2028 was directed for determination, deadline 2026-06-30 passed without a public determination) pulled ~500 kt into US warehouses and roughly doubled US refined imports, taking COMEX from ~80 kt to ~650 kt. Tariffs, sanctions and rerouting are commodity-supply-security's row - this policy is used ONLY to explain the LOCATION of inventory, which is mine. Directional logic: bullish for the ex-US clearing price, NOT bullish for world scarcity. FALSIFIER: resolve the tariff question in a way that frees US metal to move and the aggregate read wins and this tightness disappears quickly. Vendor contrast, labelled tier-5 estimate and not an official balance: a bank view revised from ~+490 kt global surplus (April) to a -640 kt deficit OUTSIDE the US (June).

MODULE_RULES 9 opacity treatment APPLIED, not described. Hidden stocks are explicitly NOT inferred to be zero: every cover figure emitted by this orb (12.3 days total, 7.4 days on-warrant, 3.7 days ex-US) is a LOWER BOUND on the true global buffer, which is 968.4 kt PLUS an unmeasured quantity of bonded, off-warrant and off-exchange material. China bonded-zone stock: unmeasured - reachable SMM bonded articles could not be pinned to 2026 with confidence (returned figures ~55.5 kt and ~219.8 kt, a factor of four apart) and were EXCLUDED rather than cited stale; that dispersion is itself the evidence. LME off-warrant: unmeasured, no report obtained. ICSG considers the bonded effect material enough to publish a seasonally adjusted Q1 balance (386 kt) beside the headline (396 kt), but the bonded STOCK LEVEL is not held at all. Demonstrated dispersion among figures I could source: SHFE warrant 56.7 kt vs SHFE weekly warehouse 70.1 kt (24% apart, different definitions); a 'US strategic stockpile >1 Mt' claim that may restate the 676 kt already counted at COMEX; the refined-balance headline failing its own components by 221 kt. Consequence for the synthesis: primary-source coverage is effectively 0% (zero accepted vintages) and dispersion is far above 15%, which is HIGH opacity and caps the supply-demand directional-conviction score at 45 - the synthesis applies the cap, I record the inputs. Because bonded stocks alone have historically run in the tens to low hundreds of kt, the unmeasured tail is plausibly the same order as the entire ex-US visible buffer, making the ex-US tightness read the most fragile conclusion in this module.

Copper's analogue to central-bank buying is STATE strategic stockpiling, and it is this orb's row (one fact, one owner). China: the state-backed China Nonferrous Metals Industry Association publicly called for more copper in national strategic stockpiles and for state-owned producers to build commercial inventories, after a price rally in early Feb-2026; copper sits with cobalt, nickel and lithium in state reserve expansion plans. HARD LIMIT ON THIS ROW: SRB purchase timing and tonnage are treated as confidential and are not published, so NO tonnage can be cited and none is inferred - inferring one would breach the section 9 ban on assuming hidden stocks. Evidence is headline-level via a search summary, not the article. Direction bullish, strength deliberately low, unquantified in tonnes, cannot carry weight in either horizon.

The qualifying/opposing fact, emitted separately so it cannot be quietly absorbed. One secondary source estimates the US strategic copper stockpile has passed 1,000 kt, 'the largest national reserve outside China'. I do NOT treat this as incremental demand. Reason: 1 Mt sits uncomfortably close to the ~676 kt already counted in COMEX warehouses plus private trader inventory, and the source does not define whether it means a GOVERNMENT reserve, exchange stocks, or all US-located metal. Read as a government reserve it is new demand; read as all US metal it double-counts the visible stocks in the inventory-buffer rows. Under CLAUDE.md 4 the conservative reading wins, so this row is neutral and exists to cap the row above rather than to add to it.
